title: Contaminant movement around a permeable reactive barrier at Solid Waste Management Unit 12, Naval Weapons Station Charleston, North Charleston, South Carolina, 2009
citation: Vroblesky, D.A., Petkewich, M.D., and Conlon, K.J., 2010, Contaminant movement around a permeable reactive barrier at Solid Waste Management Unit 12, Naval Weapons Station Charleston, North Charleston, South Carolina, 2009: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report SIR-2010-5086, map scale 1:1,176.
notes:
Groundwater-contamination report for one site (SWMU12). Pages 1-36 are front matter, text, and contaminant-distribution figures; the figure pages hold concentration labels without readable geologic content and were not extracted. No named stratigraphic units are described in this packet. Hydrogeologic framework recorded as groundwater entries. Lithologic logs of piezometers appear in later appendixes.
Pages 37-38: summary and reference list; only references about South Carolina sites or data were recorded (general remediation, sampling and mineralogy references from other places were skipped). Page 40: well-construction table (Appendix 1) recorded as well label, State Plane coordinates, installation date and ground elevation; screen depths not recorded (no schema field). Pages 41-45: monthly water-level altitudes (ft rel. NAVD 88); only the 8/28/2009 synoptic row was recorded per well. Pages 46-49: organic-compound concentrations (Appendix 3) not extracted; table continues into the next packet. 12MW-10S has no 8/28/2009 measurement.
Pages 50-62 are all Appendix 3 (concentrations of organic compounds in groundwater and surface water, August 2000 to September 2009), continued from the previous packet. The table holds only water-chemistry results by well and date (including marsh surface-water sites), which have no field in the extraction schema; nothing was extracted. No lithology, units, structures or hydrogeologic values on these pages.
Pages 63-75 are all Appendix 4 (concentrations of inorganic constituents and field properties in groundwater, August 2000 to September 2009). The table holds only water-chemistry results by well and date (alkalinity, major ions, iron, sulfate, sulfide, pH, specific conductance, temperature, turbidity), which have no field in the extraction schema; nothing was extracted. No lithology, units, structures or hydrogeologic values on these pages.
Pages 76-77 finish Appendix 4 (inorganic water chemistry) and page 78 is Appendix 5 (VOC concentrations in temporary wells 12TW-2009-01 to -47, August-October 2009); water-chemistry results have no schema field and were not extracted. Pages 79-82 (Appendixes 6-9, lithologic logs and well-construction diagrams of piezometers 12PZ-07 to 12PZ-10, attributed to Terry Environmental Services, written commun., 2009) contain only their captions in the text layer; the logs themselves are images and were not readable here. These four pages need OCR or a visual read to capture the lithologic intervals. Page 84 is the back cover.
Re-read of appendix 6-9 piezometer logs (12PZ-07 to 12PZ-10). Descriptions quoted from the OCR text; interval tops and bottoms read off each log's depth scale at the boundaries drawn in the lithology pattern column of the 150-dpi tiles (image values, inferred, approximate). TOP OF CASING ELEVATION, EASTING and NORTHING are printed as 0 (placeholders) and were not recorded; no vertical datum printed. Moisture, odor and PID columns and well-construction intervals (casing, screen, bentonite, grout, filter) are not recorded as geologic values; screen intervals: 12PZ-07 11-16, 12PZ-08 10-15, 12PZ-09 13-18, 12PZ-10 10-15 FT BGS.
Compact water-test tables, one row per printed table line; columns paired by token order (18 value cells per row in Appendixes 3-4, 8 in Appendix 5); column order and units checked on page images of pp. 46 and 63. Parameters are the printed column abbreviations (legend expansions in each column note); values kept as printed with qualifiers and flags (<, J estimated, B blank, H holding time, M poor recovery); "---" (not measured/collected) left blank. Site IDs ending in R are replicate samples (legend "R, replicate sample"), kept as printed. Marsh surface-water sites (East Marsh Site 1-3, North Marsh Site 1-3) are a separate table of kind "other". Rows skipped because the text layer has fewer cells than columns (a cell is missing, so positions are ambiguous): p. 47 12MW-03SR 8/29/2001; p. 47 12MW-03S 1/14/2004; p. 49 12MW-04S 2/10/2009; p. 52 12MW-10S 1/14/2004; p. 53 12MW-10S 11/27/2007; p. 54 12MW-13S 1/30/2006; p. 55 12MW-17S 1/13/2004; p. 57 12MW-21S 9/13/2005; p. 57 12MW-22D 1/12/2004. These need a page-image re-read.

These need a page-image re-read. On p. 61 the 11DCE cell of 12MW-28S 2/11/2009 is a bare "," in the text layer (digits lost); left blank, to be read from the page image.

Site IDs ending in R are replicate samples (legend "R, replicate sample"), kept as printed. Marsh surface-water sites (East Marsh Site 1-3, North Marsh Site 1-3) are a separate table of kind "other".
